methodology: Every factual claim on this site is backed by an official government source, statute, regulation, or court rule. Claims in progress are marked pending. This registry is updated as sources change.

sources.claim: Veterans Crisis Line is reachable by calling 988, then pressing 1.
SAMHSA National Helpline is 1-800-662-4357.
sources.source_name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration

sources.claim: VA provides mental health and substance use treatment services for enrolled veterans.
VA Community Care under the MISSION Act can authorize care from community providers.
Substance use history alone does not automatically bar VA disability compensation; the disability must still be service-connected under 38 C.F.R.  3.301.
Many states and counties operate Veterans Treatment Courts. Specific programs vary by jurisdiction.
sources.source_name: Local court or Veterans Service Organization
sources.notes: BJA's www.bja.gov domain does not resolve from this environment; bja.ojp.gov/programs/veterans-treatment-courts returns 404; justiceforvets.org blocks automated requests. Veterans Treatment Courts are well-documented DOJ-funded programs, but the canonical URL in this entry is currently unreachable from automated verification. Leave PENDING until a verified DOJ/BJA landing page is found.

sources.claim: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) is a monthly benefit for surviving spouses and children when a veteran's death resulted from a service-connected condition.
The Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) is a DoD annuity for survivors of military retirees.
sources.source_name: Defense Finance and Accounting Service / DoD Military Pay

sources.claim: CHAMPVA provides health coverage for eligible survivors who cannot use TRICARE.
The Fry Scholarship provides Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits to children and spouses of service members who died in the line of duty after September 10, 2001.
Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA, Chapter 35) provides education benefits to dependents of veterans with certain service-connected disabilities or deaths.
Surviving spouses may have options regarding an existing VA-guaranteed home loan.
VA-accredited representatives and Veterans Service Organizations can help survivors file claims.
USAA is a private financial services association open to eligible military members and families; it is not a government agency.
State and local veterans resource information varies by jurisdiction and should be confirmed with the relevant state veterans affairs office or state court.
sources.source_name: LEGAL HELP 4 VETS State Resources Methodology

sources.claim: King James Version (KJV) Bible text is in the public domain in the United States.
sources.source_name: Library of Congress / general public-domain status

sources.claim: VA Form 21-526EZ is used to file an original claim for VA disability compensation.
VA Form 21-4138 (Statement in Support of Claim) is used for lay statements and buddy statements.
VA Form 20-0995 is used for a Supplemental Claim with new and relevant evidence.
VA Form 20-0996 is used for Higher-Level Review of a VA decision.
VA Form 10182 is used to appeal to the Board of Veterans' Appeals.
VA Form 21-0966 is used to file an intent to file a claim, preserving an earlier effective date.
VA Form 20-10206 is used to request personal records including the C-file.
VA Form 21-8940 is the current Veteran's Application for Increased Compensation Based on Unemployability.
VA Form 21-4192 is the current Request for Employment Information in Connection with Claim for Disability Benefits used with Individual Unemployability claims.

Total Disability based on Individual Unemployability (TDIU) allows veterans who cannot maintain substantially gainful employment to be paid at the 100% rate even if their combined rating is less than 100%.
The PACT Act expands VA health care and benefits for veterans exposed to burn pits, Agent Orange, and other toxic substances.
VA may schedule a compensation and pension (C&P) exam to evaluate a disability claim.
VA provides a discharge upgrade wizard and instructions for service members and veterans seeking to upgrade their discharge characterization.
Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) provides housing counseling and temporary financial assistance to veterans and their families.
HUD-VASH combines HUD housing vouchers with VA supportive services for homeless veterans.
Veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness can call the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 1-877-4AID-VET (1-877-424-3838).
Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) provide income to disabled individuals who meet medical and work/credit requirements.
The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) provides food benefits to eligible low-income individuals and families.
The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA), 50 U.S.C.  3901 et seq., provides financial and legal protections to active-duty servicemembers.
sources.source_name: Code of Federal Regulations / Department of Justice

sources.claim: The Fair Housing Act, 42 U.S.C.  3604(f), prohibits discrimination and requires reasonable accommodations for disabilities in housing.
sources.source_name: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development

sources.claim: VA has a statutory duty to assist claimants in obtaining evidence relevant to a claim.
VA may conduct a Character of Discharge (COD) review to determine whether a veteran's discharge is a bar to VA benefits.
Discharge Review Boards (DRB) and Boards for Correction of Military/Naval Records (BCNR) can upgrade or correct military discharge records.
sources.source_name: Department of Defense / Military Department Boards

sources.claim: Each VA medical center has a Patient Advocate to help resolve concerns about VA health care.
Veterans may request assistance from their U.S. Representative or Senator's office with federal agency issues.
sources.source_name: U.S. House of Representatives / U.S. Senate

sources.claim: 38 C.F.R. Part 3 contains VA regulations on adjudication of disability claims, including duty to assist and presumptive conditions.

15 U.S.C. § 1692g requires specified validation information from covered debt collectors and gives a consumer a 30-day validation period; a timely written dispute or original-creditor request requires the debt collector to cease collection of the disputed debt until the statutory verification/original-creditor information is mailed.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: VA Form 26-1880 is used to request a Certificate of Eligibility for a VA home loan.
VA Form 21P-527EZ is the current Application for Veterans Pension.
VA Form 21P-534EZ is used to apply for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC), Survivors Pension, and/or accrued benefits.
VA Form 22-5490 is used to apply for Fry Scholarship or DEA (Chapter 35) education benefits.
VA Form 10-10EZ is used to apply for enrollment in the VA health care system.
VA Form 21-2680 is the current Examination for Housebound Status or Permanent Need for Regular Aid and Attendance.
VA Form 26-4555 is used to apply for a Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant for veterans with certain severe service-connected disabilities.
VA home loans are backed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and available to eligible veterans, service members, and surviving spouses.
VA Pension provides tax-free monthly payments to wartime veterans with limited income and net worth who meet age or disability requirements.
CHAMPVA is a comprehensive health care program for qualifying spouses and children of veterans who are rated permanently and totally disabled or died from a service-connected condition.
Children of servicemembers who died in the line of duty generally must be between 18 and 26 years old to use Fry Scholarship benefits, with certain exceptions.
VA education benefits under the GI Bill and related programs require enrollment certification by a school and may be subject to overpayment if enrollment changes.
VA burial benefits may include a gravesite in a national cemetery, headstone or marker, burial flag, and Presidential Memorial Certificate for eligible veterans.
VA-accredited attorneys, claims agents, and Veterans Service Organizations can represent claimants before VA.
Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grants help veterans with certain service-connected disabilities adapt or buy a home.
211 is a free information and referral service that can connect people to local emergency shelter, food, and housing resources.
Social Security survivor benefits may be available to surviving spouses and dependent children of workers who paid into Social Security, including veterans.
VA provides substance use disorder treatment including detoxification, residential rehabilitation, outpatient care, and medication-assisted treatment for eligible veterans.
Under the MISSION Act, veterans may be referred to community care when VA cannot provide timely or accessible substance use treatment.
Veterans Treatment Courts are specialized dockets that combine treatment and supervision for eligible veterans in the criminal justice system.
sources.source_name: Justice For Vets / Bureau of Justice Assistance
sources.notes: Automated requests to this authoritative site receive HTTP 403; the site is known to be live and accessible to normal users. Status reflects verified authoritative source, not automated reachability.

sources.claim: VA offers support services for caregivers of veterans, including education, respite care, and mental health resources.
Unemployment Compensation for Ex-Servicemembers (UCX) provides unemployment benefits to eligible former members of the Armed Forces.
USCIS may grant parole in place to certain noncitizen spouses, children, and parents of U.S. military members, allowing them to remain in the U.S. while seeking adjustment of status.
Certain servicemembers and veterans may naturalize under INA 328 or 329, including posthumous naturalization for servicemembers who died during qualifying service.
USCIS Form N-400 is the Application for Naturalization.
USCIS Form N-426 is a Request for Certification of Military or Naval Service used in military naturalization applications.
USCIS Form I-130 is the Petition for Alien Relative used to establish a qualifying family relationship.
USCIS Form I-485 is the Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status.

The Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) allows certain abused spouses, children, and parents of U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents to self-petition for immigration status without the abuser's participation.
Immigration enforcement policies may include considerations for military veterans; veterans facing removal may seek legal counsel and administrative relief.
VA chaplain services provide spiritual and pastoral care for veterans, families, and staff, regardless of religious affiliation.
Under 38 U.S.C.  5107(b), VA must resolve reasonable doubt in the veteran's favor when evidence is in approximate balance.
sources.source_name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs / Cornell Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: VA assigns disability ratings based on symptoms at different points in time; staged ratings may apply when symptoms worsen or improve over time.
INA 328 covers naturalization for servicemembers with at least one year of honorable service; INA 329 covers naturalization for servicemembers who served during periods of hostilities.
Veterans have the right to a decision review if they disagree with a VA decision on their claim.
VA Claims Intake Center in Janesville, WI processes paper decision review requests by mail.
Board Appeals offer Direct Review, Evidence Submission, or Hearing options with different timelines and evidence rules.
After requesting a decision review, VA will mail a decision packet; status can be checked online or by calling 1-800-827-1000.
VA provides an online discharge upgrade wizard to help veterans determine which board to apply to based on branch of service and discharge type.
The Department of Defense Electronic Reading Room provides contact information for Discharge Review Boards (DRB) and Boards for Correction of Military/Naval Records (BCM/NR).
sources.source_name: Department of Defense / Boards of Review

sources.claim: VA can provide benefits to veterans with a discharge that is not honorable if VA determines the discharge was under conditions other than dishonorable (Character of Discharge review).
The Board for Correction of Naval Records (BCNR) reviews Navy and Marine Corps records correction requests and discharge upgrades.
The Army Board for Correction of Military Records (ABCMR) reviews Army records correction requests and discharge upgrades.
The Air Force Board for Correction of Military Records reviews Air Force records correction requests and discharge upgrades.
sources.source_name: U.S. Department of the Air Force

sources.claim: The Coast Guard Board for Correction of Military Records reviews Coast Guard records correction requests and discharge upgrades.
VA pension provides monthly payments to wartime veterans with limited income and net worth who meet age or disability requirements.
VA pension benefits are reduced or eliminated when countable income exceeds the maximum annual pension rate (MAPR).

Total Disability based on Individual Unemployability (TDIU) pays compensation at the 100% disability rate when a veteran cannot secure substantially gainful employment due to service-connected disabilities.
The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) caps interest at 6% on pre-service debts and provides lease termination and eviction protections.

CFPB explains validation notices and the 30-day dispute period for covered debt collectors; a timely written dispute can require collection activity on the disputed amount to pause until verification is provided.
Unemployment Compensation for Ex-Servicemembers (UCX) provides unemployment benefits to former military members based on state law.
State veteran benefits vary by state; veterans should contact their state veterans affairs office or department of veterans services.
The LEGAL HELP 4 VETS Legal Library provides plain-language explanations of legal terms, statutes, and sample letters for veterans and advocates.
The LEGAL HELP 4 VETS Advocate Toolkit provides templates, trackers, and checklists for organizing veteran cases and communicating with agencies.
Consumers can file complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau about debt collection, mortgage, or credit issues.
sources.notes: Automated requests to this authoritative site receive HTTP 403; the site is known to be live and accessible to normal users. Status reflects verified authoritative source, not automated reachability.

sources.claim: The VA White House Hotline receives complaints and inquiries about VA services and benefits.
The VA Office of Inspector General hotline accepts reports of fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement.
Legal Services Corporation funds local legal aid offices that provide free civil legal help to low-income Americans including veterans.
Every VA medical center has a Patient Advocate to help resolve care concerns.
The National Legal Aid & Defender Association and LSC-funded programs provide civil legal aid.
The National Law Center on Homelessness & Poverty publishes legal tools and eviction defense resources.
sources.source_name: National Law Center on Homelessness & Poverty

sources.claim: The VA Foreign Medical Program covers service-connected disabilities and conditions for veterans living abroad.
Justice For Vets supports Veterans Treatment Courts across the country.
sources.source_name: Justice For Vets / Bureau of Justice Assistance
sources.notes: Automated requests to this authoritative site receive HTTP 403; the site is known to be live and accessible to normal users. Status reflects verified authoritative source, not automated reachability.

sources.claim: Social Security can waive overpayments if repayment would be against equity and good conscience or the recipient is without fault.
VA fiduciaries manage VA benefits for beneficiaries who cannot manage their own financial affairs.

VA Debt Management Center handles collection and assistance for VA benefit overpayments and specified education debts; health-care copay bills and VA-guaranteed home-loan servicing use different VA/servicer routes.

VA education-debt guidance distinguishes school liability for specified tuition/fee/Yellow Ribbon overpayments from student liability for specified housing, books, and allowance debts; dispute, waiver, and repayment options depend on who owes the debt and the notice/process.
SCRA protects servicemembers from vehicle repossession without a court order if the loan was originated before active duty and the servicemember made a deposit or payment.
sources.notes: Automated requests to this authoritative site receive HTTP 403; the site is known to be live and accessible to normal users. Status reflects verified authoritative source, not automated reachability.

sources.claim: Beneficiaries or others can report fiduciary misuse to the VA Fiduciary Hub; VA can investigate, suspend, or remove a fiduciary.

VA beneficiaries may request waiver of covered benefit overpayment debt under current waiver law. Waiver depends on statutory/regulatory conditions; fault is an equity-and-good-conscience factor, while fraud, misrepresentation, or bad faith can bar waiver.

VA current debt guidance separates an informal debt dispute from appeal/review of the underlying benefit decision or a waiver decision; the applicable written decision and review-rights notice control the appeal route and deadline.
Feeding America operates a nationwide network of food banks searchable by zip code.
The National Coalition for Homeless Veterans connects veterans to emergency and transitional housing providers.
VA facilities and some jurisdictions have victim-witness coordinators who can help veterans report fraud or abuse.

VA Form 10-1394 (not 10-1393) is the Application for Associated Health Benefits for Transitional Health Care Members; VA uses various forms for records requests, and veterans can also use the online VA Blue Button/health records portal.
The National Personnel Records Center (NPRC) stores official military personnel, health, and medical records of discharged and deceased veterans of all services during the 20th century.
DoD uses DD Form 149 (Application for Correction of Military Record) for Board for Correction of Military Records applications.
VA Vet Centers provide community-based counseling, outreach, and referral services to eligible veterans and their families.
50 U.S.C. § 3931 protects servicemembers against default judgments in civil actions while in military service.
sources.source_name: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: 50 U.S.C. § 3932 allows servicemembers to request a stay of civil proceedings when military duties materially affect their ability to appear.
sources.source_name: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: 50 U.S.C. § 3937 limits qualifying pre-service obligations to 6% interest during military service; qualifying mortgage-type obligations remain capped for one year after service, while qualifying nonmortgage obligations use the military-service period. A servicemember generally must provide written notice and qualifying military-service documentation no later than 180 days after termination or release from military service. Excess interest is forgiven, not deferred.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: 50 U.S.C. § 3951 restricts eviction of servicemembers and their dependents from leased premises when monthly rent is below a statutory cap and a court order is obtained.
sources.source_name: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: 50 U.S.C. § 3953 restricts foreclosure and sale of real property owned by servicemembers before entering military service.
sources.source_name: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: VA provides resources to help veterans with VA-backed home loans avoid foreclosure, including contacting the loan servicer and requesting loss mitigation.

42 U.S.C. § 3604 prohibits discrimination in the sale or rental of housing, including discrimination based on disability, and requires covered housing providers to grant reasonable accommodations when necessary and reasonable.
sources.source_name: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: HUD's Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity office enforces the Fair Housing Act and provides guidance on housing discrimination, including disability discrimination and reasonable accommodations.
sources.source_name: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development

sources.claim: VA's current Manage VA Debt hub separates benefit overpayments and copay bills, explains dispute and financial-help options, and states that the ordinary waiver request window is one year from the first debt letter or copay bill.
VA debt notices explain the debt, the reason for the debt, and options for payment or dispute/waiver.
VA maintains frequently asked questions about VA debt, including who can sign in, what debts can be viewed, and how to request help.
VA allows veterans to request a waiver of certain benefit overpayment debts when specific legal conditions are met.
VA offers payment options for benefit overpayments and copay bills, including online payment through pay.gov and payment by mail or phone.
Veterans can dispute a VA debt if they believe the debt is incorrect, providing an explanation and supporting evidence.
VA Debt Management Center can be contacted by phone or mail for questions about benefit overpayments.

Current 38 U.S.C. § 5302 provides a one-year ordinary application period for waiver of recovery of covered VA benefit overpayments, subject to statutory extension where notice was not actually received within a reasonable period; waiver is barred by specified fraud, misrepresentation, or bad-faith conditions.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: The Treasury Offset Program (TOP) collects federal and state payments to satisfy delinquent debts owed to federal agencies and states, including some VA debts that have been certified for collection.
sources.source_name: Bureau of the Fiscal Service / U.S. Department of the Treasury

sources.claim: VA forms, including forms used in debt and waiver processes, can be found on the official VA forms website.
Veterans can pay VA copay and benefit overpayment bills online through Pay.gov using the VA Debt payment form.
sources.source_name: Pay.gov / U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4301 states the purposes and sense of Congress for USERRA, including the non-discrimination and prompt reemployment principles.
sources.source_name: U.S. Congress / Cornell Legal Information Institute
sources.notes: USERRA purposes and congressional findings. Verified 200.

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4311 prohibits discrimination, denial of employment, or adverse employment action against persons because of their membership, application for membership, performance of service, application for service, or obligation to serve in the uniformed services.
sources.source_name: U.S. Congress / Cornell Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4312 establishes USERRA reemployment eligibility, advance-notice rules and exceptions, the cumulative service limit and statutory exceptions, and different report/application timing based on service length and circumstances.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4313 establishes the priority rules for the reemployment position, including the escalator position and qualification/requalification alternatives.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4316 addresses seniority and other rights/benefits during and after uniformed service and includes limited just-cause protection after qualifying reemployment.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4317 provides health-plan continuation and reinstatement rules, including up to 24 months of continuation coverage subject to statutory conditions and cost rules.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4321 authorizes the Secretary of Labor to provide assistance to persons claiming rights under USERRA, including through DOL VETS.
sources.source_name: U.S. Congress / Cornell Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4322 governs enforcement of USERRA employment or reemployment rights through administrative and judicial remedies, including DOL VETS referral to the Department of Justice and private actions.
sources.source_name: U.S. Congress / Cornell Legal Information Institute

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4323 governs enforcement against State and private employers, including DOL referral to the Attorney General and private enforcement routes.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: 20 C.F.R. Part 1002 contains the Department of Labor's USERRA implementing regulations for private, State, and local employment, including eligibility, notice, service limits, reemployment position, benefits, and enforcement assistance.
sources.notes: Legacy source ID retained to avoid broken anchors; the prior registry incorrectly identified the USERRA regulations as 29 C.F.R. Part 100.

sources.claim: The DOL elaws USERRA Advisor is an official Department of Labor interactive tool that helps servicemembers and employers understand USERRA rights and obligations.

DOL Veterans' Employment and Training Service (VETS) administers USERRA assistance, investigates complaints, and may refer matters to the Department of Justice for enforcement against State or private employers.
sources.notes: Canonical DOL VETS USERRA page. Returns 403 to automated requests but is live for users.

sources.claim: The Department of Justice Civil Rights Division Employment Litigation Section enforces certain servicemembers' employment rights, including cases referred by DOL VETS under USERRA.
sources.notes: Current DOJ Civil Rights employment page. Direct USERRA sub-URL changed; this is the current authoritative landing page.

sources.claim: Employer Support of the Guard and Reserve (ESGR) provides informal assistance, education, and ombudsman services to help resolve USERRA-related disputes between servicemembers and employers.
sources.source_name: Employer Support of the Guard and Reserve
sources.notes: Verified 200; automated SSL verification failed but site is accessible to users.

sources.claim: DOL publishes a USERRA notice poster that employers must display, informing employees of their USERRA rights.
sources.notes: Canonical poster URL; returns 403 to automated requests but live for users.

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4318 governs pension treatment after qualifying reemployment, including continuous-service credit and employee contribution make-up timing.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4312 contains a cumulative five-year limit on the duration of service for which a person has reemployment rights with the same employer, subject to specified exceptions.
sources.source_name: U.S. Congress / Cornell Legal Information Institute
sources.notes: USERRA cumulative service limit and exceptions. Verified 200.

sources.claim: 38 C.F.R. § 1.963 implements waiver of covered non-loan-guaranty VA benefit overpayments, including the one-year application period and extension rule for delayed receipt beyond the debtor's control.

38 C.F.R. § 1.911 distinguishes informal dispute, waiver, waiver hearing, and appeal of the underlying VA decision; these rights may be exercised separately or simultaneously, and collection consequences depend on the applicable offset/collection rules.

VA's current debt-help guidance separates overpayment dispute, waiver, repayment/compromise, and appeal of the benefit or waiver decision; VA states that disputing an overpayment within 30 days of the first debt letter can avoid collection actions while VA decides the dispute.
VA Form 5655 is the current Financial Status Report used for specified waiver, compromise, and longer repayment-plan requests.
VA explains when a Financial Status Report (VA Form 5655) is required, including waiver, compromise, and repayment plans longer than five years.

38 C.F.R. § 4.16 contains the schedular TDIU percentage framework, defines marginal employment concepts, and requires extraschedular consideration/referral for veterans unable to secure and follow substantially gainful employment because of service-connected disabilities who do not meet the percentage standards.
38 U.S.C. § 1521 contains statutory Veterans Pension service requirements, including multiple wartime-service pathways; current minimum-active-duty rules must also be considered for later entrants.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: VA's current pension eligibility page distinguishes service requirements for Veterans who entered active duty before September 8, 1980 from later minimum-active-duty rules and lists current age/disability, discharge, income, and net-worth conditions.

VA's current GI Bill overpayment guidance separates school liability for tuition/fee/Yellow Ribbon overpayments from student debts such as housing/books/allowances and routes disputes through the applicable VA education/debt process.
38 U.S.C. § 4324 governs USERRA enforcement with respect to Federal executive agencies through the Merit Systems Protection Board framework.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: 38 U.S.C. § 4327 provides that no statute of limitations applies to USERRA complaints or claims filed under chapter 43, while separate reemployment report/application timing requirements remain.
sources.source_name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.claim: OSC may consider representation before the MSPB for qualifying federal executive agency USERRA complaints after DOL-VETS investigation/referral; private, State, and local employer matters use different enforcement routes.
DOJ may bring USERRA actions against private, State, and local government employers after the DOL-VETS referral process; DOJ is not the universal first-line forum for every USERRA claim.

DOJ's current SCRA guidance explains the 6% pre-service debt cap, written/documentary notice no later than 180 days after military service ends, forgiveness of excess interest, and mortgage versus nonmortgage duration distinctions.
38 C.F.R. § 1.965 defines the equity-and-good-conscience standard and factors used in VA waiver decisions after the threshold waiver requirements are met.

Military OneSource provides current Legal Services/JAG locator routing and explains that installation Legal Assistance Offices may provide legal information, paperwork help, and advice to eligible service members and families; eligibility and available services vary by office.
sources.source_name: Military OneSource / U.S. Department of Defense
sources.notes: Do not promise eligibility or representation to all veterans.

sources.claim: VA's current LSV-H program funds legal services for eligible Veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness; grantee service areas, subject-matter coverage, capacity, and eligibility vary, so listing does not guarantee representation.
sources.source_name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — Homeless Programs
sources.notes: Current FY26 grantee referral information available on source page.
